es: Diagnosticar por qué un mensaje suena brusco, frío o excesivamente rígido y elegir la corrección con marcadores de cortesía y directividad adecuada.

vocabulary.es: decir las cosas sin rodeos ni suavizar

teaching.en: Tom's message was blunt because he likes to pull no punches: «Give me the file today» is an order with no polite marker, and it can sound abrupt to a busy colleague.
teaching.es: El mensaje de Tom era brusco porque no se anda con rodeos: «Give me the file today» es una orden sin ningún marcador de cortesía y puede sonar seco a un compañero ocupado.
teaching.explanationEs: Blunt: una orden directa, sin marcadores de cortesía. Pull no punches es decir las cosas sin suavizarlas; sound abrupt describe el efecto en quien lo lee.
segments: Tom's message was blunt because he likes to pull no punches: «Give me the file today»
is an order with no polite marker, and it can sound abrupt to a busy colleague.
teaching.audioText: Tom's message was blunt because he likes to pull no punches: «Give me the file today» is an order with no polite marker, and it can sound abrupt to a busy colleague.

teaching.en: Could you send me the file when you can? I would appreciate it, especially if at all possible before lunch.
teaching.es: ¿Podrías enviarme el archivo cuando puedas? Te lo agradecería, sobre todo si fuera posible antes de comer.
teaching.explanationEs: Could you + I would appreciate it: la petición ya suena cortés. If at all possible deja margen al otro.
segments: Could you send me the file when you can? I
would appreciate it, especially if at all possible before lunch.
teaching.audioText: Could you send me the file when you can? I would appreciate it, especially if at all possible before lunch.

teaching.en: Would you mind sending me the file by noon? It asks without ordering, so nobody has to walk on eggshells around a busy colleague.
teaching.es: ¿Te importaría enviarme el archivo antes del mediodía? Pide sin ordenar, así que nadie tiene que andar con pies de plomo con un compañero ocupado.
teaching.explanationEs: Would you mind + -ing: petición indirecta y educada. Walk on eggshells es moverse con extremo cuidado para no molestar.
segments: Would you mind sending me the file by noon? It asks without
ordering, so nobody has to walk on eggshells around a busy colleague.
teaching.audioText: Would you mind sending me the file by noon? It asks without ordering, so nobody has to walk on eggshells around a busy colleague.

teaching.en: Unfortunately, I cannot attend the meeting on Friday; a good refusal will cushion the blow with a reason and an alternative.
teaching.es: Lamentablemente no puedo asistir a la reunión del viernes; un buen rechazo amortigua el golpe con una razón y una alternativa.
teaching.explanationEs: Unfortunately prepara al lector para una mala noticia; cushion the blow es suavizarla.
segments: Unfortunately, I cannot attend the meeting on Friday; a good refusal
will cushion the blow with a reason and an alternative.
teaching.audioText: Unfortunately, I cannot attend the meeting on Friday; a good refusal will cushion the blow with a reason and an alternative.

teaching.en: «I am writing to inform you that lunch is ready» sounds stiff between two colleagues, because the situation is casual and the wording is far too official: say «Lunch is ready!»
teaching.es: «I am writing to inform you that lunch is ready» suena rígido entre dos compañeros, porque la situación es informal y la redacción demasiado oficial: di «¡La comida está lista!».
teaching.explanationEs: Stiff: demasiado oficial para la situación; basta una frase sencilla.
segments: «I am writing to inform you that lunch is ready» sounds stiff between two colleagues, because
the situation is casual and the wording is far too official: say «Lunch is ready!»
teaching.audioText: «I am writing to inform you that lunch is ready» sounds stiff between two colleagues, because the situation is casual and the wording is far too official: say «Lunch is ready!»

teaching.en: To soften an abrupt «No», say «I am afraid that is not possible», and when you are in doubt, err on the side of politeness.
teaching.es: Para suavizar un «No» seco, di «Me temo que no es posible», y en caso de duda, peca de cortesía.
teaching.explanationEs: I am afraid that… suaviza un rechazo sin dar rodeos; err on the side of + nombre es inclinarse por algo por prudencia.
segments: To soften an abrupt «No», say «I am afraid that is not possible»,
and when you are in doubt, err on the side of politeness.
teaching.audioText: To soften an abrupt «No», say «I am afraid that is not possible», and when you are in doubt, err on the side of politeness.

prompt.es: ¿Qué diagnóstico encaja con este mensaje de un compañero?

choices.text: Blunt: an order with no polite marker.
Stiff: too official between colleagues.
Warm: friendly and relaxed.

feedback.es: Answer my email now es una orden sin please ni could, y el reproche posterior la endurece: suena brusca.

hint.es: Fíjate en el imperativo sin please ni could.

origin.text: Message from a colleague at nine in the morning: «Answer my email now. I have asked twice already and nobody has replied.»

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Te importaría enviarme el archivo antes del mediodía?»

feedback.es: Would you mind + -ing es una forma indirecta y educada de pedir algo.

hint.es: Es el verbo que significa «importar» o «molestar».

origin.text: I am afraid my manager needs the file before the meeting. Would you ___ sending it to me by noon?

prompt.es: Elige la corrección que suaviza el mensaje sin perder la petición.

choices.text: Send me the report by noon, please, now.
Could you send me the report by noon, please?
I formally request that you send me the report immediately.

feedback.es: Could you + please convierte la orden en una petición cortés y conserva el plazo; la versión oficial y larga se vuelve rígida y la que añade now sigue sonando a orden.

hint.es: Convierte la orden en una pregunta con could.

origin.text: Send me the report by noon.

prompt.es: ¿Qué diagnóstico encaja con este mensaje entre compañeros?

choices.text: Blunt: it gives an order without being polite.
Warm: friendly and relaxed.
Stiff: too official for such a simple message.

feedback.es: La fórmula I am writing to inform you that es oficial y resulta rígida para avisar de un café.

origin.text: I am writing to inform you that there is coffee in the kitchen, which you are welcome to drink during the break.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo suena el mensaje.

choices.text: Abrupt and unfriendly.
Direct but friendly.
Stiff and official.

feedback.es: Un No seco, una orden final y un reproche sin marcadores de cortesía dan un tono cortante.

origin.audio: No. I can't do Friday. Do it yourself. I've already told you twice, and I'm not going to repeat it.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con su efecto.

feedback.es: Cada expresión actúa en un momento distinto: pedir, dar una mala noticia, hablar sin suavizar o decidir con prudencia.

prompt.es: Diagnostica el tono del mensaje de Tom y elige la mejor corrección.

choices.text: Stiff and overly official; say: «I wish to inform you that the chairs are required at nine tomorrow.»
Blunt and angry; say: «Could you bring the chairs tomorrow at nine?»
Warm and relaxed; leave it, because the thanks softens everything.

feedback.es: El mensaje regaña y ordena sin cortesía; una petición con could lo arregla, y el agradecimiento final no compensa el reproche.

origin.text: Hi all. You forgot the chairs again. Honestly, I do not understand how a simple list can be so hard to follow, and I am getting tired of repeating myself. Bring them tomorrow at nine, and do not be late, please. If anyone has a problem with that, say so now, because I will not chase anyone afterwards. The hall will be locked at half past nine, and we have already paid for it twice this year. Thanks, Tom

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender Tom con «I will not chase anyone afterwards»?

choices.text: That he will take the job on himself if nobody answers.
That he no longer cares if the chairs arrive.
That he expects the job done without reminders.

feedback.es: Advierte de que no insistirá: espera que las sillas lleguen sin recordatorios, lo que refuerza su tono seco.

origin.text: Hi all. You forgot the chairs again. Honestly, I do not understand how a simple list can be so hard to follow, and I am getting tired of repeating myself. Bring them tomorrow at nine, and do not be late, please. If anyone has a problem with that, say so now, because I will not chase anyone afterwards. The hall will be locked at half past nine, and we have already paid for it twice this year. Thanks, Tom

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué pide la persona y cómo lo hace.

choices.text: The speaker asks politely for another day and accepts a refusal.
The speaker asks to move the meeting but insists on Monday.
The speaker announces that the meeting will be skipped without a reason.

feedback.es: Unfortunately y Would it be possible? suavizan la petición, y «if not, I completely understand» acepta un no sin presionar.

origin.audio: Good morning. Unfortunately, I can't attend Friday's meeting, as I'll be travelling. Would it be possible to move it to Monday? If not, I completely understand, and I'll read the minutes carefully. Thank you for your patience.

prompt.es: Completa: «Te agradecería que pudieras enviarlo hoy, aunque sea en borrador.»

feedback.es: La fórmula completa es I would appreciate it if you could…: sin it la frase queda incompleta.

origin.text: The report is late and the client is waiting. I would appreciate ___ if you could send it today, even in draft form.

prompt.es: Elige cómo suavizar esta respuesta seca sin cambiar el rechazo.

choices.text: That is absolutely impossible, and I will not discuss it.
I am afraid Wednesday is difficult for me, but I could do Thursday.
I formally decline your request for the reason stated above.

feedback.es: I am afraid… amortigua el rechazo y propone una alternativa; las otras dos lo endurecen o lo vuelven rígido.

origin.text: Reply from a colleague: «No. Wednesday is not possible, and I do not have time to explain.»

prompt.es: Escucha y elige para qué menciona el hablante al bebé.

choices.text: To complain about the building.
To warn that the baby may start crying soon.
To make the request easier to accept.

feedback.es: La razón sobre el bebé humaniza la petición y la hace más fácil de aceptar; no es una queja ni una invitación.

origin.audio: Would you mind keeping the noise down after ten? I'd really appreciate it. I know it's Friday, and I'm not trying to spoil anyone's evening, but the walls here let every sound through and the baby has only just gone to sleep.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase da una mala noticia con tacto?

choices.text: Unfortunately, your order will arrive late; I am sorry, and we will refund the delivery.
Your order is late. That happens sometimes, so you will simply have to wait for it.
Your order is late, and honestly that is not something I can change, so please stop asking.

feedback.es: Unfortunately, la disculpa y una compensación amortiguan el golpe; las otras dos dan la noticia sin tacto, con resignación o con dureza.
